ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graphs of the linear functions $y=kx+3$ and $y=-x+b$ intersect at point $P(2,4)$. What is the solution set of the linear inequality in $x$, $kx+3>-x+b$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Solve: When $x>2$, we have $kx+3>-x+b$,\\
which means the solution set of the inequality $kx+3>-x+b$ is $x>2$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{x>2}$.
